𝐈𝐓 𝐓𝐎𝐎𝐊 𝐌𝐀𝐑𝐓𝐈𝐍 𝐒𝐂𝐎𝐑𝐒𝐄𝐒𝐄 𝐍𝐄𝐀𝐑𝐋𝐘 𝟑𝟎 𝐘𝐄𝐀𝐑𝐒 𝐓𝐎 𝐌𝐀𝐊𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐈𝐒 𝐅𝐈𝐋𝐌⁣ 👀 
⁣
Scorsese first read Shūsaku Endō’s 1966 novel Silence in 1989, after it was given to him by Archbishop Paul Moore following a screening of The Last Temptation of Christ. The book follows two Portuguese Jesuit priests who travel to 17th-century Japan, where Christians are being persecuted, in search of their missing mentor.⁣
⁣
Scorsese became deeply interested in adapting it, particularly because its questions about faith, doubt, suffering and the apparent silence of God connected with themes he had explored throughout his career.⁣
⁣
He began seriously developing a film adaptation in the early 1990s, but the project repeatedly stalled. Financing was difficult, other films took priority, and Scorsese felt the material required the right circumstances to make properly. Various versions and casts were discussed over the years before the film finally entered production in 2015, starring Andrew Garfield, Adam Driver and Liam Neeson.⁣
⁣
𝐒𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞 (𝟐𝟎𝟏𝟔) was released in late 2016 roughly 27 years after Scorsese first encountered the novel.

source_details.title: Silence
source_details.synopsis: Silence is a 2016 epic historical drama film directed by Martin Scorsese from a screenplay by Jay Cocks and Scorsese. It is based on the 1966 novel by Japanese author Shūsaku Endō, marking the third film adaptation of the novel. The film stars Andrew Garfield, Adam Driver, Tadanobu Asano, Ciarán Hinds and Liam Neeson. The plot follows two 17th-century Jesuit priests who travel from Portugal to Edo period Japan via Macau to locate their missing mentor and spread Catholic Christianity. It is the third of Scorsese's films about religious figures struggling with challenges of faith, following The Last Temptation of Christ (1988) and Kundun (1997).
